svg.title: A Universal Union issue experience
svg.desc: A conceptual interface anatomy for an AUU issue. A plain-language status sentence and visible process bar sit above four persistent cards for scope, people, authority, and visibility. The current-stage workspace presents proposals, evidence, objections, affected perspectives, audience previews, and a challenge action. Essential, reason, and evidence layers reveal detail progressively. Eight questions define informed task completion.

text.tspan: CONCEPT INTERFACE ANATOMY · NOT A PRODUCT SCREENSHOT
AN AUU ISSUE, SEEN BY A PARTICIPANT
The interface should make scope, people, authority, visibility, consequence, and correction recoverable at a glance.
Residents are comparing three intersection designs. This process is advisory; the city council has not
delegated decision authority. Deliberation closes 14 October. Two accessibility challenges remain open.
CURRENT: DELIBERATION · NEXT TRANSITION: READINESS REVIEW · RESPONSIBLE BODY: PROCESS STEWARDS
Compare proposals without losing evidence, affected perspectives, or unresolved objections.
crossing phase · curb redesign · traffic calming
collision records · accessibility audit · cost estimates
emergency access · winter maintenance · displaced traffic
disabled pedestrians · cyclists · drivers · nearby workers
Visible to anyone; account link hidden
Why the rule exists · how status changes
THE ESSENTIAL LAYER MUST REMAIN TRUE WITHOUT OPENING THE OTHERS.
BEFORE ANY CONSEQUENTIAL ACTION, THE PARTICIPANT SHOULD BE ABLE TO ANSWER
Challenge is available at the point of the claim or action; it is not buried as generic feedback.
READY ONLY WHEN REPRESENTATIVE PARTICIPANTS CAN TEACH BACK THE CIVIC MODEL AFTER ONE ORDINARY ENCOUNTER
